groups.title: Tablet (E82600ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins E, B1 and B6 in physical tiredness, in pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after an illness and in later life. It is used for the relief of stiff shoulders and neck, numbness of the hands and feet and cold hands and feet in disorders of the peripheral circulation and at the menopause, and for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulders and the like), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, dermatitis, beriberi and tired eyes. It is also used for muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and over: take 1 tablet at a time, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 12 months of age, if you have severe kidney failure, if you have hypersensitivity to soya-bean oil or have had an allergy to it, or if you have hypersensitivity to soya or peanut.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder or a low protein level in the blood; or if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or fat emulsions must be given to you with care.
If you have a tendency to thrombosis, or if you are short of folic acid, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene.
Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, red patches, cardiac arrest (stopping of the heartbeat) or reduced function of the central nervous system occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
If a period comes earlier than expected, the bleeding gradually becomes heavier, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or oral contraceptives containing oestrogen.

Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for blocked nose, runny nose, sneezing, watering eyes, pain in the throat and a heavy feeling in the head caused by a nasal cold (acute rhinitis), allergic rhinitis or sinusitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times in 1 day, after meals. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a child under 15 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks; if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure; or if you have severe acute or chronic kidney disease or kidney failure.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have had sudden abdominal pain in connection with the pseudoephedrine component; if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, kidney disease, swelling, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are an older person; if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache; or if you have had insomnia, dizziness, weakness, tremor or palpitations with cold medicines, cough and expectorant medicines or oral medicines for rhinitis.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Do not keep taking it over a long period.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose of this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are receiving medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids or alcohol.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If haemorrhagic stroke, nausea or vomiting, thirst (persistent or severe), constipation, loss of appetite, rash or reddening, itching, difficulty passing urine, headache, facial flushing, unusual sensitivity to light, shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), pseudoaldosteronism (a fall in the amount of urine, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, a rise in blood pressure, headache and the like), muscle disease (weakness, cramps of the limbs, paralysis), or reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (a sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (D73800ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat (pain in the throat), cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it, if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine, if the user is an infant under 3 months of age, or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is an infant or young child under 2 years of age; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are an older person or physically weak; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, oedema, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like), difficulty passing urine or a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem, an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache; or if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 or have had it.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, anti-Parkinson medicines and the like), cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Do not take this medicine if you stopped taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) within the last 2 weeks.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, preparations containing potassium, preparations containing liquorice, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Do not keep taking it over a long period.
Do not drink alcohol when you take it.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
If symptoms do not improve after 5 or 6 doses, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, anti-Parkinson medicines and the like), cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are receiving other medicines such as barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants or steroids.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters), asthma, generalised weakness, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes), pneumonia with cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever, or symptoms of ischaemic colitis linked to the pseudoephedrine component (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (D38700ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule at a time, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
An overdose in a child aged 6 years or under can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep it out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have haemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism), haemosiderosis or anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis, impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder, or a low protein level in the blood. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations or antacids while you are taking this medicine. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene. Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If hives, itching, a photosensitivity reaction, abdominal or stomach pain, cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever or coma occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
